summary: Discord music can now crossfade between tracks (blending audio, not just a hard cut) -- off by default, enable with [music] crossfade_seconds in config.toml.
details: Spike, not a hardened feature: a track's outgoing audio blends into the next track's incoming audio for the configured number of seconds, via a live-mixed audio source. Only a natural track end crossfades -- /music skip stays an instant cut on purpose.
0.0 (default) means no behaviour change at all -- crossfading is entirely config-gated.
limitations: Uses the stdlib audioop module for audio mixing, which is deprecated and removed in Python 3.13 -- needs replacing before any Python upgrade past 3.12 if this becomes permanent.
Linear (not equal-power) gain ramp -- may not sound as smooth as a polished crossfade.
A track with no known duration (yt-dlp couldn't determine one) falls back to a hard cut for that boundary.
Not yet verified for real audio quality against a live Discord voice channel -- only unit-tested against synthetic timing.
